full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiff, as made out in the plaint of the suit, was that the transferees sold the suit land for a consideration of Taka 4,500.00 to the defendants by registered safkabala deeds dated 21st Baishakh, 1382 BS corresponding to 5.5.75 and delivered khas possession of the suit land to the defendant petitioners. On the same date a deed of agreement was to have been executed by the defendants for retransfer of the said land on refund of the consideration money within 10 years but after 10 years of the execution of the said documents. The plaintiff demanded the execution of the retransfer deed from the defendants on ground of the consideration money but defendants having refused to execute the transfer deed the plaintiff was compelled to file the present suit for specific performance of contract. The defendant appeared in the said suit by filing written statement wherein they, inter alia, denied to have executed any deed of agreement in favour of the plaintiff and stated that they were not liable for re-transfer of the suit land to the plaintiff. They further stated that they had already transferred the suit land to their respective wives, defendants No. 3 and 4 on 8.12.1981.
